extracted.intended_audience: researchers (faculty and research teams) preparing MURI white papers and full proposals for ARO/ONR/AFOSR funding
extracted.subtask_description: Create white papers/full proposals responsive to individual MURI topic descriptions, addressing stated objectives, research concentration areas, resource constraints, and topic-specific exclusions or incentives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective — QML with quantum sensor data
rubrics_metrics.description: To develop and explore novel QML approaches to process quantum data, and to enable enhancements over the currently best quantum and classical methods. Specifically we envision exploiting quantum sensor data to avoid QRAM complications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should focus on exploiting quantum sensor data to avoid QRAM overhead, expand understanding of data structures amenable to quantum speedups, assess scaling of gains (e.g., with ensemble size), and identify QML algorithms optimal for sensing tasks. May also inform development of enhanced classical ML.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research concentration area — QML: data types
rubrics_metrics.description: (1) fundamental analysis of the types of data best suited for QML, collected from various quantum sensors either in local or distributed configurations
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigations can include identifying which sensor-derived data structures are most amenable to quantum processing and how collection modalities (local vs distributed) affect suitability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research concentration area — QML: platform innovations
rubrics_metrics.description: (2) fundamental analysis of and innovations in QML platforms and their optimization for quantum sensing applications
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work may include algorithmic, architectural, or systems-level innovations that improve QML performance specifically on quantum-sensed inputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research concentration area — QML: classical vs quantum comparisons
rubrics_metrics.description: (3) methods for comparing fundamental operations in quantum and classical ML realms and their limitations, to better understand under what circumstances which approach is optimal
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comparative frameworks, complexity/accuracy analyses, and benchmarks that clarify regimes of advantage or parity are appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research concentration area — QML: data collection methods
rubrics_metrics.description: (4) optimal methods of collecting either static or time dependent data amenable for QML processing
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes experimental or design work on sensor measurement protocols, pre-processing, and data-ensemble design to maximize QML utility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipated resources — QML topic
rubrics_metrics.description: No more than an average of $1.5M per year for 5 years, supporting no more than 6 funded faculty researchers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should be planned within these resource expectations; deviations or larger exceptions should be discussed with topic chiefs during the white paper phase if applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective — Structural Color in Engineered Living Systems
rubrics_metrics.description: To elucidate and understand the genetic, chemical, and structural mechanisms responsible for naturally occurring structural color in bacteria and/or fungi; to use this understanding to translate naturally occurring structural color pathways and/or create novel engineered structural color systems in bacteria and/or fungi; and to engineer living bio-hybrid systems where inorganic nanomaterials are interfaced with engineered bacteria/fungi to enable external stimuli response and dynamic modulation of structural color on demand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should address mechanisms at genetic/chemical/structural levels, translation into engineered microbes, and bio-hybrid interfacing with nanomaterials for stimuli-responsiveness and dynamic modulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research concentration area — Structural color: genetic and chemical pathways
rubrics_metrics.description: (1) Elucidate the genetic and chemical pathways that are responsible for naturally occurring structural color in bacteria and fungi
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes molecular genetics, biochemical analyses, and pathway elucidation work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research concentration area — Structural color: optical-structure modeling
rubrics_metrics.description: (2) Characterize and model the relationships between optical properties and 3D structure in these microbes
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May include optical characterization, multiscale modeling, and 3D structural analysis relating morphology to optical output.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research concentration area — Structural color: synthetic biology translation
rubrics_metrics.description: (3) Explore synthetic biology approaches to translate naturally occurring structural color pathways and/or create novel engineered structural color pathways in bacteria and/or fungi to create engineered living systems displaying structural color at the single-cell and/or collective level (i.e., collective structural color of colonies and biofilms)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work can include genetic engineering, chassis translation (e.g., into E. coli or S. cerevisiae), and strategies for single-cell vs collective optical outputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research concentration area — Structural color: bio-hybrid design and tuning
rubrics_metrics.description: (4) Design, create, and characterize bio-hybrid systems where nanomaterials are interfaced with engineered bacterial and/or fungal cells to provide additional optical functionality and/or sensitivity to external stimuli like magnetic fields or chemical signals, and explore approaches to dynamically tune these systems in situ
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes interfacing strategies (plasmonic/magnetic nanoparticles), stimuli-responsiveness mechanisms, and in situ dynamic tuning experiments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipated resources — Structural color topic
rubrics_metrics.description: It is anticipated that awards under this topic will be no more than an average of $1.5M per year for up to 5 years, supporting no more than 6 funded researchers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan budgets and team sizes accordingly; HBCU/MI participation may affect eligibility for additional funds (see separate entry).

rubrics_metrics.name: HBCU/MI participation incentive (Topic 10)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications for Topic 10 are invited that include participation from eligible HBCUs/MIs; however, HBCU/MI participation is not a requirement. Applications with an HBCU/MI MURI team member may be eligible for $1.5M in total additional funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Including eligible HBCU/MI partners can make a team eligible for extra funding; teams should consult Section I definitions and consider partnership strategies if seeking the additional funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective — Large-scale Bi-directional Control for Hybrid Adaptive Networks
rubrics_metrics.description: Explore how biology transforms information for data efficient and adaptive learning, by discovering biological and mathematical control principles underlying bidirectional communication between living and non-living neural networks. Outcomes are anticipated to enable hybrid networks with energy- and data-efficient training methods, complex adaptive learning and reasoning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should target discovery of control 'languages' and principles enabling bidirectional LNN-ANN communication and adaptive computation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research concentration area — LNN dynamics
rubrics_metrics.description: 1) understanding and shaping dynamics of LNN information processing (constructed in-vitro cultured networks)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work may include experimental LNN construction, measurement of dynamics, and methods to shape those dynamics for computation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research concentration area — LNN architectures for communication
rubrics_metrics.description: 2) exploring and developing LNN architectures based on mathematical and computing principles for communicating between ANNs and LNNs
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designs should enable flexible interfacing and translation between living and artificial network representations and codes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research concentration area — Data/energy optimization for training
rubrics_metrics.description: 3) new protocols and approaches for optimization of data and energy in training methods
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on training algorithms and protocols that leverage LNN adaptivity and ANN bandwidth to reduce data/energy costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research concentration area — ANN-LNN hardware emulation
rubrics_metrics.description: 4) ANN-LNN hardware emulation principles for bidirectional prediction and control
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes neuromorphic emulation frameworks (e.g., Loihi2/Lava) and hardware/software co-design to emulate bidirectional links.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research concentration area — Modular extensible ANN-LNN networks
rubrics_metrics.description: 5) modular extensible ANN-LNN networks
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work should target modular architectures that can scale and be extended for complex tasks and codes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipated resources — LNN-ANN topic
rubrics_metrics.description: It is anticipated that awards under this topic will be no larger than $1.5M per year for five years and fund no more than six faculty researchers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions warranted by specific proposal approaches should be discussed with the topic chiefs during the white paper phase of the solicitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance — discuss exceptions during white paper phase
rubrics_metrics.description: Exceptions warranted by specific proposal approaches should be discussed with the topic chiefs during the white paper phase of the solicitation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a proposed approach requires resources or structure outside the stated anticipated resources or team sizes, proposers should contact the topic chiefs early (white paper phase) to discuss justification and potential acceptability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective — Electro-momentum Coupled Piezoelectric Metamaterials
rubrics_metrics.description: This topic seeks a theoretical, computational, and experimental framework with which to design, create, understand, and dynamically tune new piezo-composite metamaterials that display EM coupling and ability to detect and precisely control elastic and acoustic wave propagation using external electric fields.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should integrate theory, computation, fabrication, and characterization to realize EM-coupled acoustic metamaterials with tunable responses to electric stimuli.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research concentration area — EM coupling theory
rubrics_metrics.description: 1) Advanced high-dimensional theory of EM coupling and general Willis coupling between elasticity, dynamics and electrostatics
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Theoretical work should map coupling physics in generalized continua and extend Willis theory as applicable to experimental platforms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research concentration area — computational design tools
rubrics_metrics.description: 2) Computational (analytic, simulation and data driven) tools to design piezoelectric metamaterials platforms (using ceramics, polymers, molecular ferroelectrics, etc.) with composition and structure maximizing EM coupling
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop simulation/design frameworks that handle multiscale heterogeneity and geometry-to-property mappings optimizing EM coupling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research concentration area — fabrication and processing
rubrics_metrics.description: 3) Piezo-composite fabrication and processing into metamaterials with complex heterogeneous architectures and multiscale features
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work should demonstrate manufacturable approaches (assembly, stacking, 3D printing, self-assembling) to produce heterogeneous piezo-composites.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research concentration area — characterization techniques
rubrics_metrics.description: 4) Novel techniques to structurally and functionally characterize EM coupled piezo-composites to elucidate underlying mechanisms and connections between material properties, design variables, and tunable EM coupling
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes microstructural mapping, measurement of EM coupling, and methods to quantify limits of tunability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research concentration area — applications in acoustic manipulation
rubrics_metrics.description: 5) Exploration of EM coupling phenomena in acoustic metamaterials for elastic and acoustic wave manipulation via external electric stimulus
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Target device-level demonstrations such as wavefront shaping, phase control, frequency/direction selective transduction, and multimodal sensitivity to pressure/velocity/electric fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipated resources — EM-coupled metamaterials topic
rubrics_metrics.description: It is anticipated that awards under this topic will be no more than an average of $1.5M per year for 5 years, supporting no more than 6 funded faculty researchers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Budget and team planning should reflect these expectations; justify deviations during white paper discussions if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective — Actuation of Polymeric Degradation via Biotoxin Recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: This MURI seeks to revolutionize the design and synthesis of a novel class of polymers or polymer assemblies that trigger rapid and selective depolymerization or disassembly via binding of a broad range of naturally occurring biomolecular agents such as toxins present in complex environments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should combine new chemistries, biomolecular recognition engineering, and modeling to enable selective, rapid, and irreversible degradation upon toxin binding while maintaining environmental stability until triggering.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research concentration area — polymer design and stability
rubrics_metrics.description: (1) Design of monomers, polymers, polymer assemblies and/or polymer-protein conjugates that are stable in harsh environments, non-toxic, and rapidly degrade upon appropriate binding
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on chemistries (self-immolating, thermodynamic depolymerization, morphological triggers) that are selective and robust in complex matrices (gut, soil, skin, contaminated environments).

rubrics_metrics.name: Research concentration area — computational multiscale modeling
rubrics_metrics.description: (2) Computational modeling at and across appropriate spatial/temporal scales to converge on design of recognition elements specific to biotoxin structures and the mechanism of initiation of depolymerization or disassembly
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes molecular dynamics, particle-based simulations, continuum multiscale models and use of ML/genetic algorithms to optimize designs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research concentration area — in vitro/in vivo complex environment analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: (3) For complex environments, in vitro and/or in vivo analysis of microbial, biochemical and physical features as a function of different conditions to direct the effective design of the polymer chemistry
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Characterization of environmental heterogeneity and its impact on polymer stability/selectivity is expected; may include model systems and operando testing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research concentration area — structural biology / in silico binding analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: (4) Structural biology and/or in silico molecular-level structure analysis of biotoxin-polymeric binding complexes
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work should include structural or computational elucidation of binding modes that trigger degradation to inform design of recognition elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipated resources — polymeric degradation topic
rubrics_metrics.description: Up to $1.5M/year for 5 years to support up to six funded faculty members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions warranted by specific proposal approaches should be discussed with the topic chiefs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective — Defect Phase Dynamics
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop a mechanistic understanding of atomic scale defect 'phase' dynamics to predict how populations of heterogeneities may be manipulated via external forcings to drive mechanical, chemical, and/or thermal behaviors of bulk materials. Electromagnetic, optical, and other functional material properties are not of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should focus on defect populations, their collective behaviors as 'phases', and manipulation via mechanical/chemical/thermal stimuli. Explicitly exclude electromagnetic/optical/functional-property-focused work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research concentration area — identify/characterize defect populations
rubrics_metrics.description: (1) identifying key defect populations in model material systems, systematically characterizing the physical and chemical descriptions of population “networks,” and applying these frameworks to more complex engineering or natural systems
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes atomistic-to-mesoscale characterization with the aim of producing defect-phase representations or diagrams.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research concentration area — theory & computation to probe thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: (2) developing theoretical and computational approaches that probe thresholds for manipulating key defect phase activity via external mechanical, chemical, and/or thermal loads, and validating through select experimentation
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Modeling should predict thresholds and response maps; selective experiments should validate predicted manipulability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research concentration area — dominant defect phase networks
rubrics_metrics.description: (3) identifying dominant defect phase networks (i.e., what defect networks “drive” mechanisms?), investigate “uniqueness” of various defect populations, and develop approaches for describing interactions with other critical, interpenetrating defect systems
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work should determine which defect networks are mechanistically controlling behaviors and how multiple networks interact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research concentration area — defect flux/phase changes across regions
rubrics_metrics.description: (4) elucidating defect flux/phase changes across key regions, e.g., boundaries, surfaces and interfaces, to identify how defect (meta)stability may control bulk material behaviors
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes experiments and models of interfaces and boundaries to reveal how defect migration/flux alters macroscale material responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipated resources — defect phase dynamics topic
rubrics_metrics.description: No more than an average of $1.5M per year for five years, supporting no more than six funded faculty researchers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan proposal scope and team size within these bounds; discuss exceptions with topic chiefs during white paper phase if applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion — not of interest: electromagnetic/optical functional properties
rubrics_metrics.description: Electromagnetic, optical, and other functional material properties are not of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals focusing primarily on electromagnetic/optical/functional properties will be considered out-of-scope for this topic and should be redirected to other appropriate topics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective — Inferring Solid-Gas Interphase Responses in Transient Flows
rubrics_metrics.description: Discover path-dependent constitutive models of solid-gas interphase behaviors under non-equilibrium conditions using physics-constrained perception integrated with relevant experimental observables.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should integrate physics-constrained learning with targeted experiments to infer thermodynamically-consistent, history-dependent models of solid-gas interphases under transient, harsh environments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research concentration area — physics-constrained learning approaches
rubrics_metrics.description: (1) Physics-constrained learning approaches incorporating mechanical deformations, chemical reactions, and/or mass loss. The materials are not prescribed, however near-term outputs may include demonstrating the ability to learn behaviors of well-characterized model solid-gas systems that then enable long-term goals of inferring more complex solid-gas interphase behaviors
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply machine learning and inference techniques constrained by thermodynamics/physics to discover constitutive behaviors; start with well-characterized model systems where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research concentration area — determining key history-dependent observables
rubrics_metrics.description: (2) Determinations of key history-dependent spatiotemporal information required to bound and bias learning approaches for solid-gas interphases toward physically relevant behaviors. Research outcomes may include “operando” characterization approaches that interrogate key dynamic mechanical, thermal, and chemical behaviors under appropriate loadings, reaction conditions, and sample geometries
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify and measure the minimal/critical observables needed to constrain inference methods and design operando experiments to provide those observables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research concentration area — forward predictions with uncertainty bounds
rubrics_metrics.description: (3) Forward predictions across relevant length and time scales, incorporating uncertainty bounds for given solid-gas systems and non-equilibrium conditions to validate inferred models. Long term outputs may include frameworks for ensuring inferred models converge to the experimental uncertainties
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deliver predictive models with quantified uncertainty that can be validated against experiments and scaled across length/time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipated resources — solid-gas interphase topic
rubrics_metrics.description: No more than an average of $1.50M per year for five years, supporting no more than six funded faculty researchers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions warranted by specific proposal approaches should be discussed with the topic chiefs during the white paper phase of solicitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: HBCU/MI participation incentive (Topic 15)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications for Topic 15 are invited that include participation from eligible HBCUs/MIs; however, HBCU/MI participation is not a requirement. Applications with an HBCU/MI MURI team member may be eligible for $1.5M in total additional funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Including eligible HBCU/MI partners may make teams eligible for extra funding; consult Section I for definitions and eligibility rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective — Quantum Simulators for Materials Design
rubrics_metrics.description: The objective of this MURI is to study materials properties at the microscopic level using quantum simulator platforms and model systems implemented on them to gain new fundamental insights into the mechanical, thermal, and/or vibrational behavior of materials. A secondary objective is to use quantum simulator platforms to accelerate the iterative process of identifying and designing new materials with physical properties of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should leverage quantum simulation platforms to study non-electronic properties (mechanical/thermal/vibrational), benchmark against conventional methods, and translate simulator insights into improved computational/experimental materials design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research concentration area — theoretical design approaches
rubrics_metrics.description: (1) theoretical approaches (computational and analytical) to design real or model materials
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes development of models and inverse design methods suitable for quantum simulator studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research concentration area — experimental quantum simulation techniques
rubrics_metrics.description: (2) experimental quantum simulation techniques and platforms to explore materials properties and behavior
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work should use or develop simulator platforms (atoms, optical lattices, engineered interactions) to probe target materials phenomena.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research concentration area — tools to extract materials properties
rubrics_metrics.description: (3) theoretical tools for understanding and extracting the materials properties from quantum simulations
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes data analysis, mapping simulator observables to material properties, and inference algorithms for extracting physical parameters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research concentration area — materials fabrication & benchmarking
rubrics_metrics.description: (4) materials fabrication and characterization techniques for benchmarking simulation results and realizing new materials designs
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should include plans to fabricate/characterize real materials to benchmark and validate simulator predictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research concentration area — incorporate simulator insights into computational materials science
rubrics_metrics.description: (5) incorporating insights and data from quantum simulators into computational materials science techniques to improve fidelity, functionality, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work should close the loop by using simulator data to enhance classical computational methods (e.g., DFT, MD) and design workflows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipated resources — quantum simulators topic
rubrics_metrics.description: It is anticipated that awards under this topic will be no more than an average of $1.5M per year for up to 5 years, supporting no more than 6 funded faculty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Budget and team composition should align with these limits; justify and discuss exceptions with topic chiefs if necessary.
